Approximately 300 ml of each concentration was placed into clean crystallization dishes (Cole Parmer, 100 mm x 50 mm) and the dishes arranged in the field of view of the hyperspectral imagers as shown in Figure 2 and Figure 3. Illumination was provided by two sets of three halogen lightbulbs (Ecosmart™, 72W), shining behind a photography diffuser umbrella, arranged opposite the hyperspectral cameras at ~38 in from the algae samples as illustrated in Figure 2. Single-point reflectance spectra were collected using a dual-channel spectrometer arrangement like previously published (2), but with different spectrometers. Two spectrometers (StellarNet, Inc. Blue Wave) were equipped with two 100-um diameter fibers (Ocean Optics, QP-100-2-UV/VIS), one equipped with a cosine corrector (Ocean Optics, CC-3) and pointed upwards at the illumination and is hereafter referred to as the downwelling fiber and the other pointed at the surface of the algae, hereafter referred to as the upwelling fiber. Spectra were acquired from each dish individually via SpectraWiz software (StellarNet, Inc.). The downwelling integration time was 2100 ms, while the upwelling integration time was either 1000 ms or 1800 ms for P. celeri and 1400 ms for N. gaditana. Each experiment had a dish containing water to estimate the bottom surface reflection (300 mL total volume at a culture depth of 4.8 cm). Calibration files were taken under the same illumination using a diffuse reflectance target (Labsphere, USRT-99-100). All spectral measurements were based on the average of 25 scans. A snapshot hyperspectral imager (Cubert, Ultris H5) equipped with the relay lens option and a c- mount lens (Headwall Photonics, 25mm F/L Telecentric VNIR Lens, f/2.5) was focused on the algae containers at a standoff distance of ~58 in. Dark and white calibrations were performed as per manufacturer’s instructions. Hyperspectral image acquisition was accomplished using the CUVIS UltrisTouch software (v2.9.1) running under Windows 11 on a laptop (HP Elitebook 1050 G1 with an Intel(R) Core™ i7-8850H CPU @ 2.60GHz processor, 16 GB of RAM, and an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 graphics card). Hyperspectral data were acquired of the scene with an integration time of 250 ms and ~100 images were collected for each scene. Dark and white calibrations were performed as per manufacturer’s instructions. Hyperspectral data were acquired of the scene with a single line integration time of 200 ms.
